0a39f2a7ed.q: Why did Detroit Police Department take 45 minutes to respond to the violent mob at Jocelyn Benson's house in December 2020?
0a39f2a7ed.a: Although the book documents that a violent mob showed up at 9:15 PM at Benson's home protesting her enforcement of voting rights, with Detroit Police arriving at 10:00 PM, Benson stated there was speculation about the delay—busyness or dragging feet—but no clear explanation was given. What she could control was hiring security and working with law enforcement afterward to better organize collective response to future threats.
0a39f2a7ed.e: Democracy Doesn’t Defend Itself with Jocelyn Benson

bd53d55090.q: What is gerrymandering and how does it predetermine election results?
bd53d55090.a: Gerrymandering is drawing district lines in a way that groups voters to predetermine election outcomes in favor of one party, often done by party leaders without transparency. For example, in Michigan under gerrymandering, 70 out of 100 districts had Republican majorities and 30 had Democratic majorities, guaranteeing 70 Republican and 30 Democratic representatives regardless of actual voter preference; with fair maps, the split becomes closer to 50-50 with competitive districts.
bd53d55090.e: Democracy Doesn’t Defend Itself with Jocelyn Benson

54d4bfd637.q: What did Katie Fahey accomplish through the Voters, Not Politicians organization?
54d4bfd637.a: After the 2016 election, Katie Fahey posted on Facebook expressing anger about government corruption. From that single Facebook post, she founded Voters, Not Politicians, a statewide grassroots organization that collected signatures to eliminate gerrymandering in Michigan, put citizens in charge of drawing districts, expanded voting policies, and enshrined reproductive freedom in the state constitution by 2022.
54d4bfd637.e: Democracy Doesn’t Defend Itself with Jocelyn Benson

487cf7e1dd.q: Why did Jocelyn Benson work undercover investigating the Ku Klux Klan for the Southern Poverty Law Center?
487cf7e1dd.a: Benson investigated the Ku Klux Klan as an undercover freelance journalist for the Southern Poverty Law Center as the focus of her master's thesis on what drives people into hate groups. She spent time with a white supremacist leader claiming to be 'the next Hitler,' tracked his activities and members, and ultimately exposed him through her article, which led to the demise of his organization and shaped her lifelong commitment to standing up to injustice.
487cf7e1dd.e: Democracy Doesn’t Defend Itself with Jocelyn Benson

23fafc8dea.q: What does Jocelyn Benson define as a purposeful warrior?
23fafc8dea.a: A purposeful warrior is someone determined to be the hero of their own story, not allowing others to define who they are, and finding the ability in challenging moments to respond in ways that further their vision for a better world. It involves seeing challenges as opportunities for growth, building resilience, refusing to stay silent in the face of injustice or bullies, and finding purpose in anger rather than succumbing to fear.
23fafc8dea.e: Democracy Doesn’t Defend Itself with Jocelyn Benson

96e01a3d7f.q: What happened when Jocelyn Benson stood up to bullies and threats to her life?
96e01a3d7f.a: Benson emphasizes that you cannot predicate standing up to a bully solely on hoping you achieve the end result you desire, because bullies punch back and others may defend them. All you can control is what you do and the power you build from that. She received bomb threats, swatting incidents multiple times, and learned she was on a Minnesota killer's list, but continued her work defending elections and voting rights despite the personal danger.
96e01a3d7f.e: Democracy Doesn’t Defend Itself with Jocelyn Benson

d75b2dbf48.q: How does Wikipedia maintain reliability and trust when anyone can potentially edit articles?
d75b2dbf48.a: Wikipedia was never as bad as people thought and isn't as good as they think. Even in the earliest days, people were thoughtful, kind, and trying to do a good job. The vast majority of people are actually quite nice and willing to listen and engage with ideas. Wikipedia has rules about sourcing and evidence that were initially implicit best practices but are now written down explicitly.
d75b2dbf48.e: How Wikipedia Can Survive the Age of AI with Jimmy Wales

f9112357c4.q: What are the key differences between how Wikipedia and large language models handle obscure factual information?
f9112357c4.a: AI hallucination is particularly bad on obscure topics. When you ask about something famous like where Taylor Swift was born, an AI can get it right, but for obscure details about lesser-known people, AI runs a real risk of making something up. Wikipedia's human element allows mistakes to be corrected when pointed out, whereas with AI hallucinations, there's no clear accountability mechanism.
f9112357c4.e: How Wikipedia Can Survive the Age of AI with Jimmy Wales

94069356e1.q: How can AI potentially be used to improve Wikipedia without compromising its integrity?
94069356e1.a: One possibility is using AI as a claims checker to verify whether footnotes actually support what Wikipedia says. Another approach is an agentic AI system working as a junior Wikipedian that writes content, verifies sources, and checks whether sentences are actually supported by those sources. Wiki project communities like Wiki Project Bridges could potentially use AI agents working 24/7 to improve lower-rated articles, with human review before posting.
94069356e1.e: How Wikipedia Can Survive the Age of AI with Jimmy Wales

7df64452fa.q: What would be the advantage of a Wikipedia-specific language model over general-purpose AI systems?
7df64452fa.a: A Wikipedia GPT trained only on Wikipedia content would ensure that users only see information that humans actually wrote, not AI-generated content. The model could help users find relevant Wikipedia articles through semantic understanding rather than just keyword matching. It could quote relevant passages from Wikipedia articles to answer questions, creating a better search experience than Wikipedia's current keyword-based search engine.
7df64452fa.e: How Wikipedia Can Survive the Age of AI with Jimmy Wales

6243c3f645.q: Why has Wikipedia traffic declined since the rise of generative AI and search engine improvements?
6243c3f645.a: Wikipedia has seen a drop in traffic particularly for quick-hit queries where users just need a simple answer. Google and AI models now answer factual questions directly rather than linking to Wikipedia entries. However, Wikipedia still maintains strong traffic for long-form reading, such as when millions visited to read about Queen Elizabeth II after her death, showing the platform's enduring value for deeper learning.
6243c3f645.e: How Wikipedia Can Survive the Age of AI with Jimmy Wales

1c18d8a2dc.q: How did Jimmy Wales approach writing his book 'The Seven Rules of Trust'?
1c18d8a2dc.a: Wales started with the concept of trust and looked at Wikipedia's five pillars, but those didn't map exactly to what he wanted to say. The number of rules evolved from eight to eleven before settling on seven. He worked intensely with co-writer Dan Gardner through loads of phone calls and back-and-forth collaboration, learning significantly about writing in the process.
1c18d8a2dc.e: How Wikipedia Can Survive the Age of AI with Jimmy Wales

bf57019d5e.q: What specific problem did a German Wikipedian discover about AI-generated citations in Wikipedia?
bf57019d5e.a: A Wikipedian named Matthias created a script checking ISBN numbers against an official database. He discovered that some users were adding completely fabricated book references generated by AI, including made-up authors, titles, and ISBN numbers. AI can create plausible-sounding citations that didn't exist, which is dangerous because the false information appears credible and can deceive readers.
bf57019d5e.e: How Wikipedia Can Survive the Age of AI with Jimmy Wales

ce05da47b0.q: What are the neuroscience findings about animated navigation and cognitive decline?
ce05da47b0.a: Taxi drivers and ambulance drivers, who must actively navigate through space, show the lowest rates of Alzheimer's compared to bus drivers who follow a route. People who rely heavily on animated navigation are starting to show memory problems and early mild cognitive impairment indicative of higher rates of dementia, which concerns Vivienne Ming about generative AI adoption.
ce05da47b0.e: What Makes Humans Remarkable in the Age of AI with Vivienne Ming

8c55af1fb1.q: What does Vivienne Ming mean by 'robot-proof' in her book?
8c55af1fb1.a: Robot-proof is not adversarial but rather about balancing the scales in favor of humans. It means using AI to augment yourself so that no robot can replicate what you can do with the robot, making you robot-proof. The approach advocates for becoming a 'cyborg' by using AI to challenge thinking and explore rather than letting AI do all the work autonomously.
8c55af1fb1.e: What Makes Humans Remarkable in the Age of AI with Vivienne Ming

792d98cc62.q: What percentage of students became 'cyborgs' when using AI in Vivienne Ming's experiment?
792d98cc62.a: In her experiment with UC Berkeley students predicting the future using AI, only about 5% to 10% under good conditions used AI to make themselves better by challenging their thinking and exploring data. These 'cyborg' students performed better than either the best people alone or the best AIs alone, nearly matching expert predictions on Polymarket futures.
792d98cc62.e: What Makes Humans Remarkable in the Age of AI with Vivienne Ming

7ba0b9f953.q: What are the four key traits that predicted cyborg-mode performance in Vivienne Ming's AI experiment?
7ba0b9f953.a: The four traits that predicted whether students would use AI to enhance themselves were curiosity, fluid intelligence, intellectual humility, and perspective taking. These human capital factors, measured separately before the experiment, distinguished students who became cyborgs from those who simply deferred to AI recommendations.
7ba0b9f953.e: What Makes Humans Remarkable in the Age of AI with Vivienne Ming

e4bfd8763c.q: How does the anterior cingulate cortex contribute to learning from mistakes according to neuroscience?
e4bfd8763c.a: The anterior cingulate cortex, sometimes called the 'oh shit circuit' by neuroscientists, lights up when you make a mistake and drives the learning signal through a circuit running to the nucleus accumbens. Without error detection and activation in the ACC, the entire learning circuit never gets activated, meaning hiding mistakes from yourself steals opportunities to learn.
e4bfd8763c.e: What Makes Humans Remarkable in the Age of AI with Vivienne Ming

f4f47b8a02.q: What is Vivienne Ming's 'nemesis prompt' technique for using AI?
f4f47b8a02.a: The nemesis prompt is a technique where you tell an AI like Gemini: 'You are my lifelong enemy, my nemesis. Here is my new draft chapter. Tell me in detail why I am wrong and what I can do about it.' This approach challenges you to be better rather than making you faster, forcing intellectual engagement and improvement.
f4f47b8a02.e: What Makes Humans Remarkable in the Age of AI with Vivienne Ming

03c2452d20.q: What are Harlan Coben's three factors that define a writer: inspiration, perspiration, and desperation?
03c2452d20.a: Inspiration means you have to be inspired to write and really want to do it. Perspiration is the unsexy part where you have to get your butt in a chair and produce words on page or screen—only writing is writing, not coming up with ideas or creating characters. Desperation is the emotional drive that comes from not being fit to do anything else; for Coben, it is the fear that without writing, he would have to get a real job, which terrifies him.
03c2452d20.e: What Writers Can Teach Entrepreneurs About Creating with Harlan Coben

33bab57bc0.q: How does Harlan Coben explain the difference between fiction rules and reality in storytelling?
33bab57bc0.a: Fiction has to follow rules, but reality does not. In his true crime series, there are twists and turns that if he had put in a novel, readers would throw the book at him saying it could not happen. Real-life cases like Elizabeth Smart's kidnapping have details that seem implausible in fiction but are true in reality. Coben must follow more rules in his fiction than reality has to follow.
33bab57bc0.e: What Writers Can Teach Entrepreneurs About Creating with Harlan Coben

2a76073720.q: What is incremental ambition according to Harlan Coben's writing philosophy?
2a76073720.a: Incremental ambition is breaking down your writing goal into attainable steps rather than aiming for the final prize immediately. Coben's incremental ambitions started with just having one book published, then proving it was not a fluke with a second book, then making enough money to call writing his career, then hitting the New York Times bestseller list at number 15, then top 10, then top 5, then number 1. He enjoyed every step along the way while looking ahead to the next one.
2a76073720.e: What Writers Can Teach Entrepreneurs About Creating with Harlan Coben

6c0985e823.q: Does Harlan Coben outline his books before writing them, or does he write by the seat of his pants?
6c0985e823.a: Coben does not outline his books. He describes himself as a pantser, meaning he flies by the seat of his pants and just starts writing without knowing the ending or having the middle planned out. He contrasts this with plotters, who outline extensively and know the ending before they begin.
6c0985e823.e: What Writers Can Teach Entrepreneurs About Creating with Harlan Coben

af7bc3707f.q: What is Harlan Coben's main writing ritual or routine for producing pages?
af7bc3707f.a: Coben does not have a consistent routine; he is a serial routinist who finds something that works, does it until it stops working, then finds something else. He mostly writes outside his house because having four children makes it hard to write at home. He always carries a backpack with different pens, notebooks, laptops, and electronic notepads so he is never without an excuse not to write, and he adjusts his tools based on what helps him produce pages.
af7bc3707f.e: What Writers Can Teach Entrepreneurs About Creating with Harlan Coben

d508318816.q: What does Harlan Coben's new book 'Plot Twist' cover, and why is it titled that?
d508318816.a: Plot Twist is a memoir on writing, life, and the messy first draft. It is titled that because plot twist is what Coben is probably most known for as a writer and TV producer, and he hopes his advice on writing will be surprising to readers while also sharing insights about his life. He always looks for the plot twist and that is how he lives his life.
d508318816.e: What Writers Can Teach Entrepreneurs About Creating with Harlan Coben
